newsitem.title: USA: US FERC outlines oversight in company realignments.
newsitem.headline: US FERC outlines oversight in company realignments.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday said while it does not have jurisdiction over mergers of public utility holding companies, it will oversee dispositions of public utility facilities that result from such mergers.
The commission said this includes transfers of control of power marketer "paper" facilities such as documents and records, as well as physical facilities such as transmission lines.

In cases where merging holding companies each own one or more public utilities, there may also be direct or indirect merger of facilities under FERC's jurisdiction, which the commission said gives it a separate basis for oversight.

The commission outlined the policy when considering the proposed mergers of Pacific Enterprises, parent of Southern California Gas Co., and ENOVA Corp, parent company of San Diego Gas and Electric Co, and of NorAm Energy Corp, a gas company, and Houston Industries Inc, which has an electric utility.
The commission claimed jurisdiction in these cases, but said it will act on the applications themselves later.
In another case involving Morgan Stanley Group and Dean Witter, Discover & Co, the commission approved the disposition of power marketer facilities.

In that case it gave permission for control of MS Capital and CHI Power Marketing Inc, power marketers with ties to Morgan Stanley, to pass to the the new company, Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co.
The commission said while it was claiming jurisdiction over new types of corporate alignments, it would try to process cases quickly.
